nodes.name: Monotone and maximally monotone operator
nodes.statement: A set-valued operator $M\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$ with graph $\gra M=\menge{(x,x^*)\in\XX\times\XX^*}{x^*\in Mx}$ is monotone if \begin{equation} (\forall (x_1,x_1^*)\in\gra M)(\forall (x_2,x_2^*)\in\gra M)\quad \pair{x_1-x_2}{x_1^*-x_2^*}\geq 0, \end{equation} and maximally monotone if, furthermore, there exists no monotone operator from $\XX$ to $2^{\XX^*}$ the graph of which properly contains $\gra M$.
nodes.statement_short: An operator is monotone when $\pair{x_1-x_2}{x_1^*-x_2^*}\geq 0$ on its graph, and maximally monotone when its graph admits no proper monotone extension.
differentia: there exists no monotone operator from $\XX$ to $2^{\XX^*}$ the graph of which properly contains $\gra M$.

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: {\bfseries Notation.} The symbols $\weakly$ and $\to$ denote respectively weak and strong convergence. The set of weak sequential cluster points of a sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\NN}$ is denoted by $\WC(x_n)_{n\in\NN}$. The closed ball of center $x\in\XX$ and radius $\rho\in\RPP$ is denoted by $B(x;\rho)$. Let $M\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$ be a set-valued operator. The domain of $M$ is $\dom M=\menge{x\in\XX}{Mx\neq\emp}$, the range of $M$ is $\ran M=\menge{x^*\in\XX^*}{(\exi x\in\XX)\,x^*\in Mx}$, and the set of zeros of $M$ is $\zer M=\menge{x\in\XX}{0\in Mx}$. $\Gamma_0(\XX)$ is the class of all lower semicontinuous convex functions $f\colon\XX\to\RX$ such that $\dom f=\menge{x\in\XX}{f(x)<\pinf}\neq\emp$. Let $f\colon\XX\to\RX$. Then $f$ is coercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}f(x)=+\infty$ and supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}f(x)/\|x\|=+\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Fixes notation: weak/strong convergence, weak cluster points, domain, range and zeros of an operator, the class $\Gamma_0(\XX)$, coercivity and supercoercivity.

nodes.name: Properties of the Kuhn-Tucker set
nodes.statement_short: $\boldsymbol{Z}$ is a closed convex subset of $\mathscr{P}\times\mathscr{D}$, equals an intersection of half-spaces $\boldsymbol{H}_{a,b}$, and is weakly-strongly closed.

conclusions: For every $\mathsf{a}=(a,a^*)\in\gra A$ and $\mathsf{b}=(b,b^*)\in\gra B$, set $\boldsymbol{s}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}^*=(a^*+L^*b^*,b-La)$, $\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\pair{a}{a^*}+\pair{b}{b^*}$, and $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}= \menge{\boldsymbol{x}\in\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}} {\pair{\boldsymbol{x}}{\boldsymbol{s}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}^*} \leq\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}}$. Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item $(\forall\mathsf{a}\in\gra A)(\forall\mathsf{b}\in\gra B)$ $[\,\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}} =\boldsymbol{0}\;\Leftrightarrow\; \boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}} =\XXX\;\Rightarrow\;(a,b^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z} \;\text{and}\;\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=0\,]$. \item $\boldsymbol{Z}=\bigcap_{\mathsf{a}\in\gra A} \bigcap_{\mathsf{b}\in\gra B} \boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}$\,. \end{enumerate}

Let $(a_n,a_n^*)_{n\in\NN}$ be a sequence in $\gra A$, let $(b_n,b_n^*)_{n\in\NN}$ be a sequence in $\gra B$, and let $(x,y^*)\in\XXX$. Suppose that $a_n\weakly x$, $b_n^*\weakly y^*$, $a_n^*+L^*b_n^*\to 0$, and $La_n-b_n\to 0$. Then $(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.

nodes.statement_short: $H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(x,y)$ is the closed affine half-space onto which $y$ is the Bregman projection of $x$, and $Q^{\boldsymbol{f}}$ projects $x_0$ onto an intersection of two such half-spaces.

nodes.name: Bregman-Haugazeau outer approximation scheme
nodes.statement: Let $\XXX$ be a reflexive real Banach space, let $\boldsymbol{f}\in\Gamma_0(\XXX)$ be a Legendre function, let $\boldsymbol{C}$ be a closed convex subset of $\overline{\dom}\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\cap\intdom\boldsymbol{f}\neq\emp$, let $\boldsymbol{x}_0\in\intdom\boldsymbol{f}$, and set $\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}=P_{\boldsymbol{C}}^{\boldsymbol{f}} \boldsymbol{x}_0$. At every iteration $n\in\NN$, find $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}\in\inte\dom\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})$ and set \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{x}_{n+1}=Q^{\boldsymbol{f}} \big(\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}\big). \end{equation} Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item $(\forall n\in\NN)$ $\boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n)$. \item $(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\NN}$ is a well-defined bounded sequence in $\intdom\boldsymbol{f}$. \item Suppose that, for some $n\in\NN$, $\boldsymbol{x}_n\in\boldsymbol{C}$. Then $(\forall k\in\NN)$ $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+k}=\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}$. \item $\sum_{n\in\NN}D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1}, \boldsymbol{x}_n)<+\infty$. \item $(\forall n\in\NN)$ $D^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2},\boldsymbol{x}_n)\leq D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1},\boldsymbol{x}_n)$. \item $\sum_{n\in\NN}D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}, \boldsymbol{x}_n)<+\infty$. \item $[\,\boldsymbol{x}_n\weakly\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}$ and $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_n)\to\boldsymbol{f} (\overline{\boldsymbol{x}})\,]$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n, \overline{\boldsymbol{x}})\to 0$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\WC(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\NN}\subset\boldsymbol{C}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Coercive and bounded set-valued operator
nodes.statement: Let $\XX$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\XX\neq\{0\}$ and let $M\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$. Then $M$ is \emph{coercive} if \begin{equation} (\exi z\in\dom M)\quad \lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}\inf\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{Mx}}{\|x\|}=\pinf, \end{equation} and it is \emph{bounded} if it maps bounded sets to bounded set.

nodes.name: Sufficient conditions for coercivity
nodes.statement: Let $\XX$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\XX\neq\{0\}$ and let $M\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$. Suppose that one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item $\dom M$ is nonempty and bounded. \item $M$ is uniformly monotone at some point $z\in\dom M$ with a supercoercive modulus: there exists a strictly increasing function $\phi\colon\left[0,+\infty\right[\to\left[0,+\infty\right]$ that vanishes only at $0$ such that $\lim\limits_{t\to+\infty}\phi(t)/t=+\infty$ and \begin{equation} (\forall (x,x^*)\in\gra M)(\forall z^*\in Mz)\quad \pair{x-z}{x^*-z^*}\geq\phi(\|x-z\|). \end{equation} \item $M=\partial\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is a supercoercive function in $\Gamma_0(\XX)$. \end{enumerate} Then $M$ is coercive.

nodes.statement_short: Bounded domain, uniform monotonicity with supercoercive modulus, or being the subdifferential of a supercoercive function each force $M$ to be coercive.

nodes.name: Coercivity of a sum with a monotone operator
nodes.statement: Let $\XX$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\XX\neq\{0\}$, let $M_1\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$, and let $M_2\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$ be monotone. Suppose that there exists $z\in\dom M_1\cap\dom M_2$ such that \begin{equation} \lim\limits_{\|x\|\to+\infty}\inf\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{M_1x}}{\|x\|} =\pinf. \end{equation} Then $M_1+M_2$ is coercive.

nodes.name: Boundedness of sequences generated by coercive resolvents
nodes.statement: Let $\XX$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\XX\neq\{0\}$, let $M_1\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$, let $M_2\colon\XX\to 2^{\XX^*}$ be monotone, let $(x_n^*)_{n\in\NN}$ be a bounded sequence in $\XX^*$, and let $(\gamma_n)_{n\in\NN}$ be a bounded sequence in $\RPP$. nodes.name: Bregman resolvent versus Moreau's proximity operator
nodes.statement: Let us note that, even in Euclidean spaces, it may be easier to evaluate $(\nabla h+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}$ than the usual proximity operator $\prox_{\gamma\varphi}=(\Id+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}$ introduced by Moreau \cite{Mor62b}, which is based on $h=\|\cdot\|^2/2$. We provide illustrations of such instances in the standard Euclidean space $\RR^m$.
nodes.statement_short: Even in Euclidean spaces $(\nabla h+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}$ may be easier to evaluate than the standard proximity operator $\prox_{\gamma\varphi}$.

nodes.name: Bregman resolvent for the Boltzmann-Shannon entropy
nodes.statement:
Let $\gamma\in\RPP$, let $\phi\in\Gamma_0(\RR)$ be such that $\dom\phi\cap\RPP
eq\emp$, and let $\vartheta$ be the Boltzmann-Shannon entropy function, i.e.,  egin{equation} \vartheta\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi\ln\xi-\xi,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RPP;\ 0,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi=0;\ \pinf,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Set $\varphi\colon(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m}\mapsto \sum_{i=1}^m\phi(\xi_i)$ and $h\colon(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m} \mapsto\sum_{i=1}^m\vartheta(\xi_i)$. Note that $h$ is a supercoercive Legendre function \cite[Sections~5 and 6]{BB97} and hence Proposition~ef{IVpp:20a}ef{IVcl:20b4} asserts that $
abla h+\gamma\partial\varphi$ is coercive and $\dom(
abla h+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}=\RR^m$. Now let $(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m}\in\RR^m$, set $(\eta_i)_{1\leq i\leq m} =(
abla h+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m}$, let $W$ be the Lambert function \cite{IVlamb96,Lamb58}, i.e., the inverse of $\xi\mapsto\xi e^{\xi}$ on $\RP$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Then $\eta_i$ can be computed as follows.  egin{enumerate} \item Let $\omega\in\RR$ and suppose that  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi\ln\xi-\omega\xi,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RPP;\ 0,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi=0;\ +\infty,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then $\eta_i=e^{(\xi_i+\gamma(\omega-1))/(\gamma+1)}$. \item Let $p\in\left[1,+\inftyight[$ and suppose that either $\phi=|\cdot|^p/p$ or  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi^p/p,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RP;\ +\infty,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then  egin{equation} \eta_i=  egin{cases} \left(\dfrac{W(\gamma(p-1)e^{(p-1)\xi_i})}{\gamma(p-1)} ight)^{ rac{1}{p-1}},&	ext{if}\;\;p>1;\[4mm] e^{\xi_i-\gamma},&	ext{if}\;\;p=1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item Let $p\in\left[1,+\inftyight[$ and suppose that  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi^{-p}/p,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RPP;\ +\infty,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then  egin{equation} \eta_i=\left( rac{W(\gamma(p+1)e^{-(p+1)\xi_i})}{\gamma(p+1)} ight)^{ rac{-1}{p+1}}. \end{equation} \item Let $p\in\left]0,1ight[$ and suppose that  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} -\xi^p/p,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RP;\ +\infty,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then  egin{equation} \eta_i=\Bigg( rac{W(\gamma(1-p)e^{(p-1)\xi_i})}{\gamma(1-p)} \Bigg)^{ rac{1}{p-1}}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $h$ the Boltzmann-Shannon entropy, $(\nabla h+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}$ is computed in closed form via exponentials and the Lambert $W$ function.

nodes.name: Bregman resolvent for the Fermi-Dirac entropy
nodes.statement:
Let $\phi\in\Gamma_0(\RR)$ be such that $\dom\phi\cap\left]0,1ight[
eq\emp$ and let $\vartheta$ be the Fermi-Dirac entropy, i.e.,  egin{equation} \vartheta\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi\ln\xi+(1-\xi)\ln(1-\xi),&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\left]0,1ight[;\ 0&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\{0,1\};\ \pinf,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Set $\varphi\colon(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m} \mapsto\sum_{i=1}^m\phi(\xi_i)$ and $h\colon(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m} \mapsto\sum_{i=1}^m\vartheta(\xi_i)$. Note that $h$ is a Legendre function \cite[Sections~5 and 6]{BB97} and that $\inte\dom h=\left]0,1ight[^m$ is bounded. Therefore, Proposition~ef{IVpp:20a}ef{IVcl:20b1} asserts that $
abla h+\partial\varphi$ is coercive and that $\dom(
abla h+\partial\varphi)^{-1}=\RR^m$. Now let $(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m}\in\RR^m$, set $(\eta_i)_{1\leq i\leq m} =(
abla h+\partial\varphi)^{-1}(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq m}$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Then $\eta_i$ can be computed as follows.  egin{enumerate} \item Let $\omega\in\RR$ and suppose that  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} \xi\ln\xi-\omega\xi,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\RPP;\ 0,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi=0;\ \pinf,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then $\eta_i=-e^{\xi_i+\omega-1}/2+\sqrt{e^{2(\xi_i+\omega-1)}/4 +e^{\xi_i+\omega-1}}$. \item Suppose that  egin{equation} \phi\colon\xi\mapsto  egin{cases} (1-\xi)\ln(1-\xi)+\xi,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi\in\left]-\infty,1ight[;\ 1,&	ext{if}\;\;\xi=1;\ \pinf,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Then $\eta_i=1+e^{-\xi_i}/2-\sqrt{e^{-\xi_i}+e^{-2\xi_i}/4}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $h$ the Fermi-Dirac entropy on $\left]0,1\right[^m$, the Bregman resolvent has an explicit quadratic-root formula.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement_short: Recast $\boldsymbol{Z}$ as $\zer(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ for a maximally monotone sum, then verify each item.

nodes.name: Setup: the operators $\boldsymbol{M}$ and $\boldsymbol{S}$
nodes.statement: Set $\boldsymbol{M}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}\to 2^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*}\colon(x,y^*)\mapsto Ax\times B^{-1}y^*$ and $\boldsymbol{S}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}} \to\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto (L^*y^*,-Lx)$. Since $A$ and $B^{-1}$ are maximally monotone, so is $\boldsymbol{M}$. On the other hand, $\boldsymbol{S}$ is linear, bounded, and positive since \begin{equation} (\forall(x,y^*)\in\XXX)\quad \pair{\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*)}{(x,y^*)}= \pair{x}{L^*y^*}+\pair{-Lx}{y^*}=0. \end{equation} Thus, it follows from \cite[Section~17]{Simo08} that $\boldsymbol{S}$ is maximally monotone with $\dom\boldsymbol{S}=\XXX$. In turn, we derive from \cite[Theorem~24.1(a)]{Simo08} that \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S}\;\text{is maximally monotone.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\boldsymbol{M}$ and the skew operator $\boldsymbol{S}$ and show their sum is maximally monotone.

nodes.name: Part (i)(a): $\boldsymbol{Z}$ is closed and convex
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12ia}: Let $(x,y^*)\in\XXX$. Then \begin{eqnarray} \boldsymbol{0}\in\boldsymbol{M}(x,y^*)+\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*) &\Leftrightarrow& 0\in Ax+L^*y^*\quad\text{and}\quad 0\in B^{-1}y^*-Lx\nonumber\\ &\Leftrightarrow& -L^*y^*\in Ax \quad\text{and}\quad Lx\in B^{-1}y^*\nonumber\\ &\Leftrightarrow& (x,y^*)\in \boldsymbol{Z}. \end{eqnarray} Therefore, we derive from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} and \cite[Lemma~1.1(a)]{IVBro65} that $\boldsymbol{Z}=\zer(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})= (\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})^{-1}(0)$ is closed and convex.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $\boldsymbol{Z}$ with $\zer(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ and invoke Browder's lemma.

nodes.name: Part (i)(b): primal and dual solution sets are projections of $\boldsymbol{Z}$
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12ib}: Let $x\in\XX$. Then $x\in\mathscr{P}\Leftrightarrow 0\in Ax+L^*BLx\Leftrightarrow (\exi y^*\in\YY^*)\; [-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\;y^*\in BLx] \Leftrightarrow (\exi y^*\in\YY^*)\;(x,y^*) \in\boldsymbol{Z}$. Hence $\mathscr{P}\neq\emp$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{Z}\neq\emp$. Likewise, let $y^*\in\YY^*$. Then $y^*\in\mathscr{D}\Leftrightarrow 0\in-LA^{-1}(-L^*y^*)+B^{-1}y^* \Leftrightarrow(\exi x\in\XX)\; [x\in A^{-1}(-L^*y^*)\;\text{and}\;0\in-Lx+B^{-1}y^*] \Leftrightarrow(\exi x\in\XX)\; [-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\; Lx\in B^{-1}y^*] \Leftrightarrow(\exi x\in\XX)\;(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of equivalences characterizing $\mathscr{P}$ and $\mathscr{D}$ through $\boldsymbol{Z}$.

nodes.name: Part (i)(c): equivalence of nonemptiness
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12ic}: Clear from \ref{ppOlk28ha12ib} (see also \cite[Corollary 2.4]{IVPe00}).
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from part (i)(b).

nodes.name: Part (ii)(a): degenerate half-spaces
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12iia} : Let $\mathsf{a}\in\gra A$ and $\mathsf{b}\in\gra B$. Then $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ [$-L^*b^*=a^*\in Aa$ and $La=b\in B^{-1}b^*$] $\Rightarrow$ $(a,b^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$. In addition, \begin{multline} \boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\pair{a}{a^*} +\pair{b}{b^*}=\pair{a}{-L^*b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}\\ =-\pair{La}{b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}=0. \end{multline} Thus $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\XXX$. Conversely, $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\XXX$ $\Rightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{a,b}=\boldsymbol{0}$ iff $\boldsymbol{H}_{a,b}=\XXX$, forcing $\eta_{a,b}=0$.

nodes.name: Part (ii)(b): $\boldsymbol{Z}$ as an intersection of half-spaces
nodes.statement_short: Prove both inclusions, using maximal monotonicity for one and monotonicity of $A,B$ for the other.

nodes.name: Part (iii): weak-strong sequential closedness
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12iii}: Set $(\forall n\in\NN)$ $\boldsymbol{x}_n=(a_n,b_n^*)$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_n^*=(a_n^*+L^*b_n^*,b_n-La_n)$. Then $\boldsymbol{x}_n\weakly (x,y^*)$, $\boldsymbol{x}_n^*\to \boldsymbol{0}$, and $(\forall n\in\NN)$ $(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_n^*)\in \gra(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$. However, it follows from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} that $\gra(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ is sequentially closed in $\XXX^{\text{weak}}\times\XXX^{*\text{strong}}$ \cite[Lemma~1.2]{IVBro65}. Hence, $\boldsymbol{0}\in(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})(x,y^*)$, i.e., by \eqref{egVxZ5y828}, $(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply sequential closedness of $\gra(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ to the shifted sequences.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: \ref{pvb8uh4504i}: Since $f$ and $g$ are Legendre functions, so are $f^*$ and $g^*$ \cite[Corollary~5.5]{Ccm01}. Therefore, it follows from \cite[Theorem~5.6(iii)]{Ccm01} that $\partial f$ and $\partial g^*$ are single-valued on $\dom\partial f=\intdom f$ and $\dom\partial g^*=\intdom g^*$, respectively. On the other hand, we derive from \eqref{epOlk28ha14} that $\dom\boldsymbol{f}=\dom f\times\dom g^*$ and that \begin{equation} \partial\boldsymbol{f}\colon\boldsymbol{\XX}\to 2^{\boldsymbol{\XX^*}}\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto \partial f(x)\times\partial g^*(y^*). \end{equation} Thus, $\partial\boldsymbol{f}$ is single-valued on \begin{equation} \dom\partial\boldsymbol{f}=\dom\partial f\times\dom\partial g^* =\intdom f\times\intdom g^*=\inte(\dom f\times\dom g^*) =\intdom\boldsymbol{f}. \end{equation} Likewise, since \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{f}^*\colon\XX^*\to\RX\colon (x^*,y)\mapsto f^*(x^*)+g(y), \end{equation} we deduce that $\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*$ is single-valued on $\dom\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*=\intdom\boldsymbol{f}^*$. Consequently, \cite[Theorems~5.4 and~5.6]{Ccm01} assert that $\boldsymbol{f}$ is a Legendre function. \ref{pvb8uh4504ii}: It follows from Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12ia} that $\boldsymbol{Z}$ is a closed convex subset of $\XXX$. Hence, since $\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\text{\rm int\,dom}\,\boldsymbol{f}\neq\emp$, we derive from \ref{pvb8uh4504i} and \cite[Corollary~7.9]{Ccm01} that $(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)=P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{\boldsymbol{Z}} (x_0,y_0^*)$ is uniquely defined.
nodes.statement_short: Separability of $\boldsymbol{f}$ gives single-valuedness of $\partial\boldsymbol{f}$ and $\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*$; uniqueness then follows from the Bregman projection theorem.

nodes.name: Part (i): $\boldsymbol{f}$ is a Legendre function

nodes.statement: (\gamma_n,\mu_n)\in\left[\varepsilon,\sigma\right] \times\left[\delta,\sigma\right]\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Pick $(\gamma_n,\mu_n)$ in the admissible box.

nodes.name: Primal Bregman resolvent
nodes.statement: a_n=(\nabla h+\gamma_nA)^{-1}\big(\nabla h(x_n)-\gamma_n L^*y_n^*\big)\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Bregman resolvent of $A$ applied to the shifted primal point.

nodes.name: Primal dual-vector
nodes.statement: a_n^*=\gamma_n^{-1}\big(\nabla h(x_n)-\nabla h(a_n)\big)-L^*y_n^* \\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Form $a_n^*$ so that $(a_n,a_n^*)\in\gra A$.

nodes.name: Dual Bregman resolvent
nodes.statement: b_n=(\nabla j+\mu_nB)^{-1}\big(\nabla j(Lx_n)+\mu_n y_n^*\big) \\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Bregman resolvent of $B$ applied to the shifted dual point.

nodes.name: Dual dual-vector
nodes.statement: b_n^*=\mu_n^{-1}\big(\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)\big)+y_n^* \\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Form $b_n^*$ so that $(b_n,b_n^*)\in\gra B$.

nodes.name: Outer-approximating half-space
nodes.statement: \boldsymbol{H}_n= \menge{(x,y^*)\in\XXX}{\pair{x}{a_n^*+L^*b_n^*} +\pair{b_n-La_n}{y^*}\leq\pair{a_n}{a_n^*}+\pair{b_n}{b_n^*}}\\
nodes.statement_short: Build the half-space $\boldsymbol{H}_n\supset\boldsymbol{Z}$ from $(a_n,a_n^*,b_n,b_n^*)$.

nodes.name: Bregman projection onto $\boldsymbol{H}_n$
nodes.statement: (x_{n+1/2},y_{n+1/2}^*)= P_{\boldsymbol{H}_n}^{\boldsymbol{f}} (x_n,y_n^*)\\
nodes.statement_short: Half-step: project $(x_n,y_n^*)$ onto $\boldsymbol{H}_n$.

nodes.name: Haugazeau update
nodes.statement_short: Full step: Haugazeau update from the reference point $\boldsymbol{x}_0$.

nodes.name: Choose the step-size pair
nodes.statement: (\gamma_n,\mu_n)\in\left[\varepsilon,\sigma\right] \times\left[\delta,\sigma\right]\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Pick $(\gamma_n,\mu_n)$ in the admissible box.

nodes.name: Primal block resolvents
nodes.statement: \text{for}\;i=1,\ldots,m\\ \left\lfloor \begin{array}{l} a_{i,n}=(\nabla h_i+\gamma_n\partial\varphi_i)^{-1} \Big(\nabla h_i(x_{i,n}) -\gamma_n\sum_{k=1}^pL_{ki}^*y_{k,n}^*\Big)\\[2mm]
nodes.statement_short: For each $i$, compute $a_{i,n}$ by the Bregman resolvent of $\partial\varphi_i$.

nodes.name: Primal block dual-vectors
nodes.statement: a_{i,n}^*=\gamma_n^{-1}\big(\nabla h_i(x_{i,n}) -\nabla h_i(a_{i,n})\big)-\sum_{k=1}^pL_{ki}^*y_{k,n}^*\\[1mm] \end{array} \right.\\[3mm]
nodes.statement_short: For each $i$, form $a_{i,n}^*$.

nodes.name: Dual block resolvents
nodes.statement: \text{for}\;k=1,\ldots,p\\ \left\lfloor \begin{array}{l} b_{k,n}=(\nabla j_k+\mu_n\partial\psi_k)^{-1} \big(\nabla j_k\big(\sum_{i=1}^mL_{ki}x_{i,n}\big) +\mu_ny_{k,n}^*\big)\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: For each $k$, compute $b_{k,n}$ by the Bregman resolvent of $\partial\psi_k$.

nodes.name: Dual block dual-vectors
nodes.statement: b_{k,n}^*=\mu_n^{-1}\big(\nabla j_k\big(\sum_{i=1}^m L_{ki}x_{i,n}\big)-\nabla j_k(b_{k,n})\big)+y_{k,n}^*\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: For each $k$, form $b_{k,n}^*$.

nodes.name: Dual residuals
nodes.statement: t_{k,n}=b_{k,n}-\sum_{i=1}^mL_{ki}a_{i,n}\\[1mm] \end{array} \right.\\
nodes.statement_short: For each $k$, set $t_{k,n}=b_{k,n}-\sum_iL_{ki}a_{i,n}$.

nodes.name: Primal residuals
nodes.statement: \text{for}\;i=1,\ldots,m\\ \left\lfloor \begin{array}{l} s_{i,n}^*=a_{i,n}^*+\sum_{k=1}^pL_{ki}^*b_{k,n}^*\\[1mm] \end{array} \right.\\
nodes.statement_short: For each $i$, set $s_{i,n}^*=a_{i,n}^*+\sum_kL_{ki}^*b_{k,n}^*$.

nodes.name: Half-space offset
nodes.statement: \eta_n=\sum_{i=1}^m\pair{a_{i,n}}{a_{i,n}^*} +\sum_{k=1}^p\pair{b_{k,n}}{b_{k,n}^*}\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Aggregate the pairings into $\eta_n$.

nodes.name: Outer-approximating half-space
nodes.statement: \boldsymbol{H}_n= \Menge{({x},{y}^*)\in\XXX} {\sum_{i=1}^m\pair{x_i}{s_{i,n}^*} +\sum_{k=1}^p\pair{t_{k,n}}{y_k^*} \leq\eta_n}\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Build $\boldsymbol{H}_n$ from the residuals and $\eta_n$.

nodes.name: Bregman projection onto $\boldsymbol{H}_n$
nodes.statement: \big({x}_{n+1/2},{y}_{n+1/2}^*\big) =P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{\boldsymbol{H}_n} ({x}_n,{y}^*_n)\\[1mm]
nodes.statement_short: Half-step projection of $({x}_n,{y}^*_n)$.

nodes.name: Haugazeau update
nodes.statement_short: Full step via $Q^{{f}}$ from the reference point.
